summary: Apartment REIT developing and operating multifamily communities in coastal supply-constrained markets. Development is a core earnings driver, so gains on sale and impairments move GAAP net income in ways Nareit FFO is designed to strip out.

annotations.ffo: The company's own reported figure, read from its 10-K MD&A reconciliation and closing on its printed "FFO attributable to common stockholders" subtotal — not the app's generic Net Income + D&A proxy. FFO is not XBRL-tagged by any REIT checked (a 10-K's label linkbase contains no such element), so the MD&A table is the only source. Each filing is accepted only when its own net-income row agrees with the net income held from XBRL for that year, which verifies the right table, the right scale and the right column alignment together; years that fail are left blank rather than filled from the proxy. AvalonBay's wording changed mid-history ("FFO attributable to common stockholders" earlier, a bare "FFO" line latterly); both are matched. Core FFO, its own adjusted measure directly beneath, is excluded.

caveats: FFO is a full replacement for the derived row, not a merge: a year the reconciliation could not verify is blank rather than falling back to Net Income + D&A, which would change the row's meaning partway across the series.
Company-specific variants in the same table (Core FFO, Normalized FFO, Adjusted FFO, Diluted FFO) are deliberately excluded; only the Nareit subtotal is carried.
